full_judgment:
This First Miscellaneous Appeal arises against the judgment and order dated 23-8-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Jhalakati in Review Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2006 (arising out of Title Appeal No. 8 of 2005) allowing the review petition upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 22-1-2006 and 27-1-2006 passing decree of declaration of Title and preliminary decree for partition of the suit land in Title suit No. 23 of 2001. 

 2. The short facts in this First Miscellaneous Appeal is that the instant respondent as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 23 of 2001 which was heard by the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Rajapur, Jhallakati. During pendency of the suit the plaintiffs filed an application for amendment of plaint under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the trial court and which was allowed by the trial court. But in spite of the amendment application being allowed, but however probably due to inadvertence of the concerned bench clerk the court's order allowing the amendment application was not duly inserted into the records. But the trial court however overlooked this significant flaw in the proceedings following laches of the bench clerk and gave its judgment and decree dated 18-1-2005 dismissing the suit without at all considering the application for amendment of plaint and also upon non consideration of its own order allowing the application. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court dated 18-1-2005 dismissing the suit without taking the application for amendment into consideration due to inadvertence of the bench clerk whatsoever, the plaintiff appellant filed Title Appeal No.8 of 2005 which was heard by the court of learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Jhalakati. During pendency of the appeal the plaintiff appellant also placed and raised the issue of non consideration of the application for amendment of plaint by the trial court before the appellate court. The appellate court upon hearing both sides passed judgment and decree dated 22- 1-2006 allowing the appeal and thereby sent the case back on remand to the trial court upon giving opportunity to the plaintiff to have the case heard upon amendment of plaint and also giving opportunity for adducing additional evidences if necessary. Against the judgment and decree of the appellate court dated 22-1-2006 the plaintiffs appellants filed a review application under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was heard by the court of learned Joint District Judge, 2nd court, Jhalakati by way of Review Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2006. Upon hearing the review petition the court passed order dated 23-8-2007 allowing the review petition upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 22-1-2006 passed by the appellate court earlier. 

 3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order dated 23-8-2007, allowing the review application the defendants in the suit being respondents in the appeal and also being respondent in Review Miscellaneous Case filed a First Miscellaneous Appeal which is before this court for disposal. 

 5. Learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the order of the review court is not sustainable and maintainable given that a review application under the facts and circumstances is not applicable in the instant case, and therefore the order of review miscellaneous case No. 2 of 2006 may be set aside. He continues his submissions upon assertion that the review court moreover acted beyond its jurisdiction upon deciding the saham and granting a preliminary decree without taking into consideration the application for amendment of plaint which was originally not taken into consideration by the trial court due to laches of the bench clerk. He submits that the appellate court correctly gave the order of remand and correctly directed the trial court to hear the matter afresh upon taking the amendment application into consideration and upon taking adducing additional evidences etc. In support of his submission that review is not maintainable in this case he cited 2 decisions of this court in the case Sree Parimal Chandra vs Mst. Shaheda Begum, reported in 20 BLD 55 = 52 DLR 206; and in the case of Kazi Shahiduddin Ahmed vs Lutfar Nahar Begum, reported in 5 MLR 321 = 5 BLC 173. He concludes his submission upon assertion that the Review Miscellaneous case No.2 of 2006 being an unlawful order therefore it may be set aside and the Miscellaneous appeal ought to be allowed for ends of justice. 

 6. On the other hand learned Advocate for the respondent submits that the review order is maintainable and the review court did not commit any error of law and therefore the review court's order need, not interfered with in this Miscellaneous Appeal. He submits that the review court has jurisdiction to correct an error of law apparent on the face of the record under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the code of Civil Procedure. He continues that in this case the appellate court committed an error of law apparent on the face of the record given that the appellate court failed to consider the amendment application and distribute the saham accordingly. He concludes his submission upon assertion that the review application being maintainable and correctly given it needs no interference and the appeal may be dismissed for ends of justice. 

 7. Heard the learned Advocate for both sides, perused the materials placed before this court including the memorandum of appeal and the judgment of all three courts below. Upon perusal it transpires that truly enough, due to laches of the bench clerk the original amendment application under Order VI, rule 17 was not taken into consideration by the trial court and the trial court therefore reached upon its finding upon overlooking this material factor. Obviously upon dismissal of the suit the plaintiff filed an appeal and placed their objection against the non consideration of the application of amendment of plaint which was allowed. It is obvious from the records that the appellate court after hearing the matter allowed the appeal and sent back the case on remand to the trial court, upon directing the trial court to hear the matter upon consideration of the amendment of plaint and upon taking further evidences if necessary. The learned Advocate for the appellant made submissions on the issue of maintainability of the review application while the respondents maintained that since there is an error apparent on the face of the record in both the judgments of the courts below, that is the trial court and the appellate court, therefore the review application is maintainable and the learned counsel for the respondent further argued that the judgment and decree by the review court granting saham to the plaintiff is correctly given. Regarding this submission of the learned Advocate my considered opinion is that it is true that there is an error apparent on the face of the record in the court of first instance, that is trial court given that the trial court upon total overlooking of the material factor of the amendment being allowed and yet not being considered gave its judgment upon absolute non consideration of this utmost significant factor. However regarding the appellate court's judgment, my considered finding is that the appellate court did not commit any 'error' which may contemplate an error apparent on the face of the record under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the code of Civil Procedure. It appears from the judgment that the appellate court allowed the appeal and sent back the case on remand upon the following terms: 

 8. I do not find any significant unlawfulness from the appellate court's order. In my considered view in this case ends of Justice can only be served upon taking into consideration the amendment of plaint under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was originally allowed by the Trial Court. Therefore the amendment of plaint must be taken into consideration including taking of evidences if necessary for a proper dispensation of justice and the judgment thereby proceeding without taking into consideration the amendment of plaint or any other materials on record cannot be allowed under any circumstances. 

 9. But however I am also of the considered view that the appellate court instead of sending back the case on remand to the trial court could have heard and disposed of the matter itself. The appellate court being the last court of facts could have heard the matter itself upon consideration of all materials on records including the amendment of plaint and adducing additional evidences if necessary. Hence I am inclined to dispose of the matter by sending the case back to the appellate court to hear the matter upon consideration of the amendment of plaint upon adducing additional evidences if necessary. 

 10. In the result, the Rule is disposed of and the judgment and order dated 23-7-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Jhalakati in Review Miscellaneous case No.2 of 2006 is hereby set aside. The appellate court being the court of learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Jhalakati is hereby directed to hear and dispose of the matter itself upon consideration of the amendment of plaint and upon adducing additional evidences if necessary. It is further directed to dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible, preferably within 6 (six) months from receipt of this judgment and order.
